chunks: Yunus narrated from Abu Thabit and Ibn 'Awn from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had a debt due from another man, and he lost him (the debtor), and did not know where to seek him, and did not know if he was alive or dead, and did not know of any heir for him, nor his lineage, nor his country. He said: 'Seek him.' He said: 'That has taken long, so shall I give it in charity?' He said: 'Seek him.'
Yunus from Fayd ibn Habib, the innkeeper

He said: I wrote to 'Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him): 'Two hundred and forty dirhams have come into my possession, and I am an innkeeper. The owner died, and I do not know of any heirs for him. What is your opinion regarding informing about its status and what I should do with it, for I have grown weary of it?' He wrote: 'Manage it and release it as charity little by little until it is exhausted.'
Yunus from al-Haytham, Abu Rawh, the innkeeper

He said: I wrote to 'Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him): 'I accept guests in the rooms, so a man stays with me and dies suddenly, and I do not know him, nor his country, nor his heirs, so the wealth remains with me. What should I do with it, and to whom does that wealth belong?' He wrote (peace be upon him): 'Leave it as it is.'

key_terms.على حاله: In its current state / Leave it as is
key_terms.مفقود: Missing person (one whose status of life or death is unknown)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for the property of a missing person whose heirs are unknown?
ai.summary: These narrations from the Chapter of the Missing Person (Mafqud) in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlight the juristic preference for preserving the missing person's wealth rather than immediate distribution. While one ruling permits gradual charity if the search for the debtor becomes unduly burdensome, the case of the innkeeper holding a guest's funds illustrates the principle of retaining the asset in trust until the heir is identified or death is confirmed, reflecting the Shia emphasis on cautious stewardship of unknown property.
